steps.title: Import required modules
steps.instruction: Import the fetch API and create a Map for tracking requests. Since we're using plain JavaScript, we'll import fetch from the global scope and declare a Map variable.
steps.hint: You don't need to import fetch as it's globally available in browsers. Just declare a Map variable to store ongoing requests.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: declaring a Map for tracking
const requestCache = new Map();

steps.title: Create a cache object to store ongoing requests
steps.instruction: Create a Map object named 'requestCache' to store promises for ongoing fetch requests.
steps.hint: Use 'const requestCache = new Map();' to create an empty Map.

// Creating a Map for storing data
const userCache = new Map();
steps.expectedOutcome: A Map object named 'requestCache' is created to track duplicate requests.
successCriteria: The code contains 'const requestCache = new Map();'

steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you create a Map object named 'requestCache'.

steps.title: Create the deduplicateFetch function
steps.instruction: Define a function called deduplicateFetch that accepts a URL and options as parameters.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The function should take two parameters: url and options.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named deduplicateFetch is defined with url and options parameters.
successCriteria: The deduplicateFetch function is defined and accepts url and options parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the deduplicateFetch function with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but check that it's named deduplicateFetch and accepts both url and options parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Make sure you create a function called deduplicateFetch that takes url and options as parameters.

steps.title: Generate a unique key for each request
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateFetch function, create a unique key by combining the URL and options parameters. Convert the options object to a JSON string using JSON.stringify() and concatenate it with the URL.
steps.hint: You can create a string like `${url}-${JSON.stringify(options)}` to generate a unique identifier for each request.
steps.expectedOutcome: The deduplicateFetch function will have a unique key generation mechanism that combines URL and options.
successCriteria: The deduplicateFetch function contains code that creates a unique string key from the url and options parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a unique key generator that will help identify identical requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to combine both the URL and stringified options into a single unique key.
steps.feedbackWrong: The unique key generation is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a string that combines the URL and JSON.stringify(options).

steps.title: Check if request is already in progress
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateFetch function, check if the request key already exists in the requestCache Map. If it does, return the existing Promise instead of making a new fetch.
steps.hint: Use the Map's has() method to check for the key's existence. If it exists, use get() to retrieve and return the Promise.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should check for duplicate requests before making new fetch calls.
successCriteria: The deduplicateFetch function checks if the request key exists in requestCache and returns the cached Promise when found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented duplicate detection logic. The function now checks if a request is already in progress before making a new one.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check if the key exists in the cache and return the existing Promise when found.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should check if the request key exists in the cache Map before proceeding. Use the Map's has() and get() methods.

steps.title: Return existing promise for duplicate requests
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateFetch function, if the request key already exists in the requestCache, return the cached promise immediately.
steps.hint: Check if the key exists in the Map using has(), then retrieve and return the promise using get().
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now return the cached promise when a duplicate request is detected, preventing duplicate network calls.
successCriteria: The deduplicateFetch function checks if the key exists in requestCache and returns the cached promise when found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the duplicate check correctly. The function now returns the cached promise when an identical request is already in progress.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're both checking if the key exists AND returning the cached promise. Use requestCache.has(key) to check and requestCache.get(key) to retrieve the promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on the duplicate check. Inside the if statement, you need to return the promise stored in the cache for that key. Use requestCache.get(key) to retrieve it.

steps.title: Make the actual fetch request for new requests
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateFetch function, after checking for existing requests, call the native fetch API with the provided url and options for new requests.
steps.hint: Use the fetch() function with the url and options parameters. This should be placed in the else block after the existing request check.
steps.analogousExample:
// Making a fetch call for new requests
const promise = fetch(url, options);
steps.expectedOutcome: The deduplicateFetch function now makes actual fetch calls for unique requests that aren't already in progress.
successCriteria: The fetch() function is called with url and options parameters inside the else block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the fetch call for new requests. This ensures unique requests actually get sent to the server.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to call fetch() with both the url and options parameters inside the else block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetch call for new requests is missing or incorrect. Remember to call fetch(url, options) inside the else block.

steps.title: Store the fetch promise in cache
steps.instruction: Inside the `deduplicateFetch` function, after the `else` block where you make the actual fetch request, store the fetch promise in the `requestCache` Map using the unique key.
steps.hint: Use the `requestCache.set(key, promise)` method to store the promise. This should be done after creating the fetch promise but before returning it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetch promise will be stored in the cache Map so that subsequent identical requests can return the same promise instead of making a new network request.
successCriteria: The `requestCache.set(key, promise)` method is called inside the `else` block to store the fetch promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully stored the fetch promise in the cache. This ensures duplicate requests will return the same promise.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're storing the actual fetch promise (not just the URL) in the cache using `requestCache.set()`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetch promise isn't being stored in the cache. Remember to use `requestCache.set(key, promise)` inside the `else` block after creating the fetch request.

steps.title: Clean up cache after request completes
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateFetch function, after the fetch promise resolves or rejects, remove the request key from the requestCache Map to prevent memory leaks.
steps.hint: Use .then() and .catch() on the fetch promise, and call requestCache.delete(key) in both success and error cases.
steps.expectedOutcome: The deduplicateFetch function will now automatically remove completed requests from the cache, preventing memory leaks from accumulating stale promises.
successCriteria: The fetch promise has .then() and .catch() handlers that both call requestCache.delete(key) to remove the key from the cache.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added cache cleanup logic. This ensures that once a request completes (whether successfully or with an error), it's removed from the cache so duplicate requests can be tracked properly in the future.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to call requestCache.delete(key) in both the success and error cases. The cleanup should happen whether the request resolves or rejects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache cleanup logic is missing. After storing the fetch promise, you need to add .then() and .catch() handlers to remove the key from requestCache when the request completes.

steps.title: Test the deduplicateFetch function
steps.instruction: Create two simultaneous test calls to deduplicateFetch with the same URL and options to demonstrate deduplication.
steps.hint: Call deduplicateFetch twice with identical arguments and log the results. You can use a mock API endpoint like 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two identical calls to deduplicateFetch return the same Promise object, demonstrating that duplicate requests are being deduplicated.
successCriteria: Two calls to deduplicateFetch with identical arguments are made and their return values are logged or compared.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully demonstrated that duplicate fetch requests return the same Promise, confirming deduplication is working.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made test calls, but ensure both calls use identical URL and options to properly test deduplication.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test calls are missing or don't properly demonstrate deduplication. Create two simultaneous calls with the same arguments.
